office_does: A Seattle Municipal Court judge hears and decides misdemeanor cases for the City of Seattle for a four-year term, deciding bail, release and diversion for many residents' only contact with the justice system.
race_blurb: An open seat (Judge Willie Gregory's term ends in January 2027). Public defender Gabe Rothstein won the primary with 54.6% over former prosecutor and Burien City Attorney Garmon Newsom (27.9%). Rothstein holds the only KCBA rating in the race and the King County Democrats' endorsement; Newsom has the Seattle Times recommendation and has raised about three times as much.

candidates.summary: Seattle Municipal Court pro tem and former Burien City Attorney with a 34-year career as a prosecutor in New York and Renton, municipal attorney and civil litigator. He is endorsed by the Seattle Times and, per his statement, incumbent Judge Willie Gregory.
highlights: Prosecutor (Bronx DA, NYC Special Narcotics, Renton Chief Prosecutor) and Burien City Attorney 2020-2026 [S4][S7]
Describes "impartial application of the law as written, grounded in precedent yet mindful of real-world impacts" [S5]
Says he will protect the community while giving defendants the opportunity for diversion, services and treatment [S1]
Seattle Times editorial board recommendation; not rated by KCBA [S7][S9]
Second in the primary (27.9%); has raised about $115,600, including $27,500 of his own money [S10][S11][S12]

judicial.basis: New since the primary: his stated philosophy is application of the law "as written, grounded in precedent," judges applying rather than making policy, and courts free of "politics and ideology". This reverses the primary's +1.

safety.basis: 34 years of prosecution and city-attorney formation with no defense practice; he states support for diversion as part of protecting the community but takes no bail position. Moved from 0 in the primary, consistent with other prosecution-formation judicial candidates.

experience.basis: Three decades of practice, pro tem service in this court and the retiring incumbent's endorsement; evidence unchanged since the primary.

candidates.summary: Public defender since 2005 with more than 70 trials to verdict, judge pro tem since 2024 and chair of the WSBA Character and Fitness Board. He won the primary outright with 54.6% and has published a position on bail.
highlights: Public defender since 2005, including drug treatment court, juvenile and civil commitment work [S1][S3]
Says release should turn on flight risk and danger, "not whether they have sufficient resources to afford bail" [S3]
Believes in "treatment, the accountability that comes with recovery, redemption, and second chances" [S1]
Rated Well Qualified by KCBA and Washington Women Lawyers [S4][S5]
First in the primary with 105,878 votes (54.6%); endorsed by the King County Democrats and The Stranger [S6][S7][S8]

judicial.basis: Calls the court "the people's court" and centers treatment, second chances and dignity; evidence unchanged since the primary.

safety.basis: Explicit position against wealth-based detention, treatment over punishment, drug-court and recovery-board service and a 20-year defense formation; re-verified on his site, unchanged since the primary.

experience.basis: Mixed: two decades of practice and a KCBA Well Qualified rating, but pro tem service only since 2024.
